text:
A: Hiya! Oh, hello! Can you hear me?
B: Alright? Yeah, loud and clear. Gareth, I'm in Taunton.
A: Sana, Bolton. Erm, sorry, can I ask, that machine behind you, is it for the hospital, like?
B: Sort of. It's a dialysis machine. My kidneys stopped working, so that does the job for them. Five times a week, four hours a go, in the spare room. Saves me trekking to the unit.
A: Oh my God. Four hours? What do you do all that time?
B: Listen to the cricket, mostly. Somerset. County cricket, so it goes on for days, which is handy really.
A: Cricket! My husband is mad for cricket. Pakistan, obviously. When Pakistan play India, honestly, nobody is allowed to talk in the house. His dad is shouting at the telly, his mum is praying. [laughs]
B: [laughs] That's the proper way to watch it. Does he play?
A: Sometimes, with his cousins in the park, tape ball. He says he's good. I don't know. [laughs] I don't understand it, the overs and everything.
B: To be fair, half of England doesn't either. I could explain it, but we've only got three minutes and I'd need about forty.
A: [laughs] That's what the engineer man said about my sister's makeup video, forty minutes. Did you talk to him? Martijn?
B: I did, first round. We were both engineers, so it was a lot of groundwater talk. Riveting stuff.
A: You're an engineer as well? Wow. Everybody in this study is so clever. I just pack parcels. [laughs]
B: Was. Civil, flood defences. Had to stop when this lot started. So at the moment I'm, erm, mostly a professional patient. Nothing wrong with packing parcels, mind. Somebody's got to, or none of us get our stuff.
A: That's true! You know, at Christmas we're so busy, everybody's ordering dresses for parties. I'm knackered, my shift got changed again this week.
B: They do that to you a lot?
A: All the time. But I swap with the girls, it's fine, I'm good at swapping. [laughs] Are you married? Sorry, is that rude?
B: No, not rude. Partner, Hannah, eleven years. Not married. We always meant to, then the kidneys happened, and there's always another appointment.
A: Aww, no! You should do it. Even small, you know, nice. I do mehndi for weddings, henna on the hands. If you were in Bolton I would do Hannah's for free, honestly.
B: [laughs] That's very kind. I'll pass it on. She'd probably like that, actually. She's always on at me to set a date.
A: Then set a date! When you get better.
B: Well, I'm on the transplant list. Two years. If that comes through, then yeah, maybe. One project at a time, you know.
A: Inshallah it comes soon. I'll pray for you. I mean it.
B: Cheers, Sana. That's kind of you.
A: Do you go out much, or no?
B: Walk the dog along the canal. Biscuit. He's old and refuses to go out in the rain, so in Somerset that's about half the year.
A: [laughs] Bolton also! He would never go out in Bolton.
